result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use deterministic tiers based on blast radius and add strong safeguards for Tier 3 actions. B does better on the prompt content: its example cards give the effect, the cluster and namespace, and say outright that the action cannot be undone. It also adds a digest that lists auto-run actions with Undo buttons, and it marks its numbers as assumptions rather than findings. A names approval fatigue as the failure more directly and adds RBAC and admission-policy backstops. However, neither answer offers real time-boxed grants scoped to a task, and A's audit log has no review or undo workflow. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers sort actions into deterministic tiers, fail closed, and use effect-first prompts. A has the stronger review loop: a digest ordered doubtful-first with undo, a skipped/denied list, status and pause controls. Its Tier 3 card also says outright that the action cannot be undone. B states most clearly why approval fatigue makes today's setup unsafe. It also adds RBAC least-privilege and admission-policy backstops that hold even when someone approves without reading, which makes the 'at least as safe' claim more convincing. Neither answer offers true task- or time-window-scoped grants beyond short-lived approvals tied to one exact command, and neither invents incident statistics.
